question: What can a deterministic offline journal/replay model classify around crash cuts, partial or torn records, restart replay, duplicates, and inaccessible evidence without claiming production durability?
title: offline synthetic crash-window / partial-write / torn-record / restart-recovery

claims.claim: The local harness deterministically classifies the 14 authored fixtures and compares fail-closed with fail-open outcomes.
Partial/torn records, missing record evidence, and inaccessible journal evidence remain UNKNOWN under fail-closed policy in the modeled cases.
claims.caveat: This is a local policy rule, not a filesystem guarantee.

claims.claim: A complete local record and success response can be classified ACCEPT by the model.
claims.caveat: ACCEPT is local model output, not proof of remote commit.

claims.claim: Conflicting payload evidence is classified REJECT by both policies in the modeled case.
Fail-open converts unresolved synthetic states to ACCEPT in most cases, illustrating a policy risk rather than a system result.
claims.caveat: The comparison is deterministic local simulation.

claims.claim: Real crash durability, filesystem ordering, remote state, exactly-once, rollback, immutable audit, and production readiness are proven by this run.
Production storage and runtime evidence are inaccessible by design.
claims.caveat: No external service, credential, or production artifact was accessed.

searched: new local fixtures, harness, validator, and manifest validator only
unresolved_conflicts: whether a remote effect occurred when local evidence is missing

limitations: Local journal/replay cannot prove real crash durability.
Cannot prove remote state, exactly-once, rollback, immutable audit, or production readiness.
